Class CashTransactionService

java.lang.Object
app.cash.CashTransactionService
@Service public class CashTransactionService extends Object
Moves the authenticated user's cash and reads their funding history.

Cash belongs to the user, not to an account: the balance is users.available_funds and every account of theirs shares it, which is why neither method takes an account id. Each movement writes the balance and appends a CashTransaction in one transaction, so the cache and its ledger cannot drift apart (BR-09/15).

Every operation is scoped to the user id from the verified token, so a caller can only read and move their own cash.

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public List<CashTransaction> getFundingHistory(UUID userId, Integer limit)
      Lists the user's deposits and withdrawals, newest first.
      Parameters:
      userId - the authenticated user's UUID from the token's sub claim
      limit - how many rows to return; null or out of range falls back to DEFAULT_LIMIT, capped at MAX_LIMIT
      Returns:
      the user's funding history, newest first

    • move

      @Transactional public CashTransaction move(UUID userId, BigDecimal amount, String reason)
      Moves money into or out of the user's cash and records it in the ledger.

      The balance row is locked before it is read, so two concurrent withdrawals cannot both pass the funds check against the same balance.

      Parameters:
      userId - the authenticated user's UUID from the token's sub claim
      amount - how much to move, positive
      reason - CashTransaction.REASON_DEPOSIT or CashTransaction.REASON_WITHDRAWAL
      Returns:
      the recorded ledger row
      Throws:
      UserNotFoundException - if the caller has not registered a profile
      AccountNotFoundException - if the caller has no account to book the row against
      InsufficientFundsException - if a withdrawal exceeds the available funds
      IllegalArgumentException - if the amount is not positive or the reason is unknown
